title: Supplier eligibility logic
scenario: Novrila Procurement is screening 22 fictitious suppliers. An order can proceed only with approval, no credit hold, lead time at most 10 days and quality score at least 95%. Separate alerts explain why a supplier needs review.

lesson.intro: Logic functions return TRUE/FALSE. Reuse IF to translate that logical result into an operational label. AND requires every condition; OR needs any condition; NOT reverses one logical result.

functions.name: AND
functions.purpose: Test that every condition is true.
functions.arguments: logical1 is the first test; optional logical arguments add tests.
functions.useCase: Require multiple release or eligibility conditions.
functions.mistake: One false condition makes the whole test false.

functions.name: OR
functions.purpose: Test that at least one condition is true.
functions.arguments: logical1 is the first test; optional arguments add alternatives.
functions.useCase: Flag any late or low-quality supplier.
functions.mistake: OR does not require both conditions to be true.

functions.name: NOT
functions.arguments: logical is one expression that evaluates TRUE/FALSE.
functions.useCase: Allow an action when a blocking condition is absent.
functions.mistake: NOT reverses the whole enclosed test; place parentheses deliberately.

lesson.combine: Use IF(AND(...), outcome1, outcome2) as a pattern on other data, then construct your own task formulas. Quote labels. A >=95 score includes 95, and <=10 includes 10. Copying a row-based formula should change the supplier row without changing its business rules.

tasks.prompt: For the first supplier, return Eligible when Lead_days is at most 10 and Quality_score_pct is at least 95; otherwise Review. Ignore approval and credit status for this task.
For the first eight suppliers, return Alert if Lead_days exceeds 10 OR Quality_score_pct is below 95. Otherwise return Clear. Keep dataset order.
For the first eight suppliers, return Allowed when Credit_hold is not Yes, otherwise Blocked. Keep dataset order and use a logical reversal.

For the first eight suppliers, return Order only when Approved is Yes, Credit_hold is not Yes, Lead_days is at most 10 and Quality_score_pct is at least 95. Otherwise return Do not order. Keep dataset order.

bonus.prompt: For the first supplier, return Escalate if it is approved but either has a credit hold or fails the lead-time/quality screen. Otherwise return Routine.
